messages:
sanjay: Quick sync — proposal to add a "cheap_path" routing mode that automatically routes requests from lower-tier customers (or accounts under token budget) to quantized/cheaper model variants. Goal: cut token $ by ~30% while keeping p50 latency and user-visible quality within an acceptable delta. Thoughts?

tara: :eyes: how do you want to surface the trigger? per-account token credits, a soft `cost_threshold`, or a per-request header?

liam: I'd prefer per-account token_budget + a percentage threshold. Example policy we'd attach to an account: ```json
{"routing":{"cheap_path":true, "budget_threshold_pct":0.25, "min_quality_drop":0.05}}
```

monica: :warning: quality regressions are the big risk. We need both (a) continuous evals on a protected prompt set and (b) a fast rollback path in the console. Also telemetry: show delta in avg tokens/req and model quality score per route.

liam: agree. Also we should expose `routing_hint` in the API so customers can opt-out per request. e.g., `x-redwood-routing: prefer_high_quality` header.

opsbot: Note: adding `routing_hint` will require API contract bump and SDK update. Opening an RFC ticket.

tara: UX on the console: add a per-customer 'Economy routing' toggle + slider for budget threshold, and new chart: 'cost saved vs. quality delta'. Recommend default OFF for mid/enterprise tiers.

monica: For rollouts, do a canary where 5% of requests from targeted accounts use cheap_path, measure: p50 latency, p95 latency, avg tokens, cost per 1k tokens, and eval failure rate. If eval failure > 1% or quality delta > configured threshold, auto-rollback.

liam: Implementation notes: smart router needs to know model compatibility (e.g., fp16 -> quantized 4-bit variant mapping). We should add a small compatibility matrix to model catalog and allow fallback mapping like `gptx-l > gptx-l-4bit`.

sanjay: Good. Also telemetry: add per-route token-cost and per-request `variant_used` to traces so billing + QA can join signals. We should avoid logging full prompts — only hashes and eval metrics.

tara: One API debate: should this routing be policy-first (console defines account policy + control plane pushes to router) or customer-first (client includes hint and server respects it)? I vote policy-first with per-request hints as overrides.

liam: policy-first makes ops simpler, yes. We'll define API surface: `account.routing_policy` + optional `X-Redwood-Routing-Hint` header. SDKs will expose `routingHint` param.

monica: Quick experiment plan: 1) Build telemetry and compatibility mapping 2) UI toggle + slider behind feature flag 3) Canary on low-risk accounts (internal + sandbox) 4) Gradual ramp with auto-rollback. Metrics dashboard: cost-saved (USD), quality-regression (%), requests routed.

sanjay: I'll draft the RFC with sample policy JSON and rollout plan. Can we get a small team to own end-to-end: @tara (console), @liam (router), @monica (eval/telemetry)?

tara: I'm in. :+1:

liam: Yup, will prep compatibility matrix entries.

monica: I'll add eval hooks and a lightweight prompt set for canary.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: eng-platform/canary at 1832146000 — will run for 2 hours.

sanjay: Thanks. Follow-ups: RFC link once posted, and a short playbook for rollback in the console.

liam: one more: let's track per-region capacity skew. If cheaper variants are only available in some regions, routing needs a region-penalty in the decision function.

monica: noted. Add `region_penalty` to policy schema.

sanjay: Great thread — will ping back with RFC and initial dashboard mock. :rocket:
